description: Non-interactive status banner. The root Alert renders a <div> with role="alert", so assistive tech announces its content as a live region when it mounts or its text changes. AlertTitle and AlertDescription are plain <div>s (AlertTitle is not a heading); neither is wired to aria-labelledby / aria-describedby automatically.

announcements: Content inside role="alert" is announced when the element appears or its text changes, without moving focus.
screenReader.notes: Because role="alert" implies aria-live="assertive", keep the message short and avoid nesting heavy interactive UI; for flows where the user must take action, prefer AlertDialog instead.

contrast.text: card-foreground over bg-card meets WCAG AA; the description uses text-muted-foreground; destructive variant uses text-destructive which also meets AA
contrast.ui: Icons use text-current, so they inherit the text colour and meet AA

motion.reducedMotion: No animations are applied by the component itself. Any enter transition comes from the consumer's animation wrapper, which should gate on prefers-reduced-motion when strict compliance matters.

consumerResponsibilities: Mount the Alert only when there is something to announce; re-rendering the same text will not re-trigger the announcement.
Use the destructive variant for errors so the color tone matches the semantic weight.
Avoid putting form fields or dialogs inside an Alert; use Dialog / AlertDialog for actionable interruptions.
